prompt: Your sponsor wants you at a 6am photoshoot, right before the hardest training day of the week.

options.label: Show up and smile for the cameras
options.text: You lose an hour of sleep, but the sponsor's rep can't stop talking about how easy you were to work with.

options.label: Beg off, protect the training day
options.text: The rep doesn't say much on the call, but you can tell they noticed.

prompt: The apparel sponsor wants you wearing their (genuinely ugly) branded hat in every interview this camp.

options.label: Wear the hat, every time
options.text: You look ridiculous in every clip, but the checks clear on time.

options.label: "Just this once" your way out of it
options.text: You dodge the hat. The sponsor's enthusiasm cools a degree.

prompt: A supplement brand wants your name on a product you've genuinely never used.

options.label: Sign it — it's just marketing
options.text: You never touch the stuff, but the deposit is real and the brand is thrilled.

options.label: Pass — you won't shill for it
options.text: You explain you'd rather keep your name on things you actually believe in. Not everyone in the room loves the answer.

prompt: A same-day signing session at the mall lands right in the middle of your camp schedule.

options.label: Rearrange the day and go
options.text: You sign a few hundred posters and eat lunch in the car on the way back to the gym.

options.label: Send your apologies
options.text: The gym gets a call from an annoyed marketing coordinator. You get your afternoon back.

prompt: The sponsor offers a logo patch on your shorts — for less money than you were hoping.

options.label: Take the deal anyway
options.text: It's not a great number, but a small check is still a check, and the relationship stays warm.

options.label: Turn it down, hold out for better
options.text: You walk away from the table. It might pay off later. It might not.

prompt: A sparring partner starts going harder than the session called for, and everyone in the room notices.

options.label: Match his intensity, no complaints
options.text: You take a beating for a round, but the room respects that you didn't back down.

options.label: Call it out and dial the pace back down
options.text: You're right to protect yourself this deep in camp, but it's an awkward silence walking to the water fountain.

prompt: Two guys are arguing over mat time again, and they both look at you to settle it.

options.label: Give up your slot to keep the peace
options.text: You lose your window, but the gym stays functional and everyone owes you one.

options.label: Hold your slot — you booked it first
options.text: You get your round in. The mood in the room takes a day or two to reset.

prompt: A young hopeful at the gym won't stop asking you for pointers, right in the middle of your own session.

options.label: Take ten minutes and actually coach him
options.text: It costs you part of your own round, but the kid — and the room — remembers it.

options.label: Politely brush him off, stay on your work
options.text: You get your full session in. He stops asking, eventually.

prompt: Your main sparring partner needs a ride across town in the middle of a training day.

options.label: Drive him yourself, eat the lost time
options.text: You lose an hour of the day, but he's the one who makes you better on fight night — that matters more than the hour.

options.label: Tell him you can't spare the time
options.text: He figures it out on his own. It's fine. It's just a little colder between you two for a while.

prompt: The coach wants to bring in a partner who badly outclasses the current sparring crew, and the room isn't thrilled about it.

options.label: Back the coach's call publicly
options.text: The new partner makes everyone better, eventually, but a couple of the old guard feel replaced.

options.label: Push back, protect the crew you already trust
options.text: The gym stays the same room it's always been. Whether that's the right call for fight night is a different question.

prompt: Your anniversary dinner falls square in the middle of fight-week prep.

options.label: Go, and make it count
options.text: You take the night off completely. It's worth every minute you don't spend visualizing the fight.

options.label: Ask to push it back a week
options.text: The understanding is real, but so is the disappointment underneath it.

prompt: Your partner wants to spend the weekend apartment-hunting instead of watching you grind through two-a-days.

options.label: Go look at apartments together
options.text: You spend the weekend picturing a life outside the gym for once. It's a good feeling.

options.label: Stay in camp, promise to make time later
options.text: "Later" is doing a lot of work in that sentence, and you both know it.

prompt: Your partner's family is in town for the week, right in the thick of camp.

options.label: Rearrange your schedule to host properly
options.text: Dinners run long and mornings start early, but everyone leaves happy.

options.label: Stay focused on camp, let them entertain themselves
options.text: You keep your training on schedule. The visit is a little quieter than anyone hoped.

prompt: Your partner asks you to skip a session for a doctor's appointment you'd otherwise miss together.

options.label: Go — this one matters
options.text: You sit in a waiting room instead of a gym, and it turns out that was exactly the right call.

options.label: Send your apologies, stay in the gym
options.text: You get the extra round in. The conversation that night is quieter than usual.

prompt: A late-night argument surfaces the same complaint again: camp is eating your whole life.

options.label: Actually stop and listen, clear tomorrow morning
options.text: You give up a session to just be present for once. It helps more than the missed reps hurt.

options.label: Explain — again — why this camp has to come first
options.text: You're not wrong about the stakes. That doesn't make the conversation land any softer.

prompt: The local paper wants a sit-down interview about your rise up the rankings.

options.label: Sit down and give them the real story
options.text: The piece runs above the fold. Your phone won't stop buzzing for two days.

options.label: Pass, keep the week quiet
options.text: You stay off the radar. Nobody outside the gym is talking about you this week.

prompt: A regional MMA podcast invites you on for a full hour, unscripted.

options.label: Take the full hour
options.text: You end up saying more than you planned to, and the clips travel further than the episode itself.

options.label: Offer a short quote instead
options.text: You keep it brief and get your evening back. The hosts sound a little disappointed on air.

prompt: A reporter tries to bait you into trash-talking your next opponent on camera.

options.label: Take the bait — give them a real quote
options.text: The soundbite gets clipped everywhere by morning. It's exactly the kind of noise that sells a fight.

options.label: Stay diplomatic, refuse to bite
options.text: It's a boring quote and a smaller headline. Your corner appreciates the restraint anyway.

prompt: A clip from your last fight goes semi-viral overnight, and your phone is full of interview requests.

options.label: Ride the wave, do the rounds
options.text: You spend the next two days doing every interview that'll have you. It's exhausting and it works.

options.label: Let it pass, stay in the gym
options.text: The clip fades from the timeline in a couple of days, same as everything else does.

prompt: Fans recognize you at the grocery store and ask for photos, right as you're trying to get home.

options.label: Stop and take every photo
options.text: It takes twenty minutes longer than it should, but every one of those people leaves grinning.

options.label: Smile, apologize, keep moving
options.text: You get home on time. Someone posts about how rude you seemed. Someone else defends you in the replies.

prompt: You tweak your knee awkwardly in live sparring, three weeks out.

options.label: Push through, finish the session
options.text: It's sore for days afterward, but you don't lose a single round of camp to it.

options.label: Shut it down for the day
options.text: You ice it, rest it, and lose the rest of the session. It's the boring, correct choice.

prompt: A nagging cough won't quit in the middle of a hard training block.

options.label: Train through it anyway
options.text: You get the work in, wheezing through the last few rounds. Nobody in camp says anything about it directly.

options.label: Take a day to actually rest
options.text: You lose a day of camp but come back breathing clean.

prompt: An old cut over your eyebrow reopens during a hard round of pads.

options.label: Tape it up, keep going
options.text: It's ugly and it stings, but you finish the round like it never happened.

options.label: Stop and get it looked at properly
options.text: The cutman closes it up clean. You lose the rest of the session to be safe.

prompt: Your hand goes numb after a long bag session, and it hasn't fully come back by morning.

options.label: Wrap it tighter, keep hitting
options.text: The feeling comes back eventually. Whether that was the smart call is a question for later.

options.label: Get it checked before doing anything else
options.text: It turns out to be nothing serious, but you lose a day of camp finding that out.

prompt: The coach spots you favoring one leg and asks, flatly, whether you should sit today out.

options.label: Tell him you're fine, keep training
options.text: You finish the session on stubbornness alone. He doesn't look convinced.

options.label: Admit it and sit the session out
options.text: The camp loses a day, but you walk out of the gym in better shape than you walked in.

prompt: The gym dues are due, and the number is bigger than you remembered.

options.label: Pay it out of your own pocket
options.text: It stings, but nobody has to know the number ever came close to a problem.

options.label: Ask the sponsor for an advance
options.text: They cover it without much fuss, but it's a favor now on the books.

prompt: Your car dies the week you need it most to get to the gym.

options.label: Pay for the repair yourself
options.text: It's an ugly bill, but the car's fixed by the next morning and camp doesn't miss a beat.

options.label: Ask the sponsor to help cover it
options.text: They front the repair cost. It's a generous move, and everyone in the room knows it's not free.

prompt: Rent's due, and the purse from your last fight still hasn't cleared.

options.label: Dip into your reserves to cover it
options.text: It's not comfortable, but it's handled quietly and the landlord never even notices.

options.label: Ask the sponsor for a short-term advance
options.text: The check arrives fast. The relationship gets a little more transactional in the process.

prompt: An unexpected medical bill lands in the mailbox mid-camp.

options.label: Cover it yourself, no complaints
options.text: The number is bad, but it's over and dealt with by the weekend.

options.label: Lean on the sponsor's wellness fund
options.text: It's exactly what the fund is for, technically. It still feels like cashing in a chip you'll want later.

prompt: Travel costs for a title-eliminator bout are steeper than the purse alone can cover.

options.label: Eat the difference yourself
options.text: You book the flights and the hotel without asking anyone for help. It's the price of the opportunity.

options.label: Ask the sponsor to pick up the travel budget
options.text: They say yes, and remind you — not for the first time — how much they've put into this camp.

prompt: A kid in the neighborhood wants a photo before school and won't stop asking about it.

options.label: Stop and make his morning
options.text: You lose ten minutes and gain one lifelong fan, loudly, in front of his whole bus stop.

options.label: Wave, keep walking to the gym
options.text: You're not rude about it, just quick. He looks a little deflated.

prompt: A fan drives three hours just to catch you leaving the gym.

options.label: Stop and give him real time
options.text: You spend half an hour talking fight strategy with a total stranger who now tells everyone he knows about it.

options.label: Sign quickly and head inside
options.text: You keep the interaction short. He posts about it anyway, a little less enthusiastically than he'd hoped.

prompt: Someone at a bar recognizes you and insists on buying a round for the whole table.

options.label: Sit down, let them buy you a soda water
options.text: It's a good half hour of stories and handshakes. Word travels through the neighborhood by the weekend.

options.label: Thank them and head home early
options.text: You keep your night short and your morning intact. Nobody's mad, exactly, just a little let down.

prompt: Gifts from fans keep piling up at the front desk, and the coach wants you to acknowledge them publicly.

options.label: Film a proper thank-you and post it
options.text: It takes a chunk of the afternoon to get right, but it lands well and people notice the effort.

options.label: Send a quick private thanks instead
options.text: It's handled, but quietly. The gesture doesn't travel any further than the front desk.

prompt: A local youth league asks if you'll guest-coach a session, and word would definitely get around.

options.label: Say yes, give them the full session
options.text: You spend an afternoon with a gym full of twelve-year-olds. Someone's parent films the whole thing.

options.label: Politely decline, protect your own training time
options.text: You keep your schedule intact. The league finds someone else, and that's fine.

prompt: Two training partners are feuding over something small, and the coach wants you to pick a side publicly.

options.label: Pick a side, settle it out loud
options.text: It becomes gym gossip for a week, but at least the tension has somewhere to go.

options.label: Stay out of it entirely
options.text: You keep the peace by refusing to engage. Both sides quietly resent that a little.

prompt: A rumor about your fight IQ — unflattering and half-true — is making the rounds at the gym.

options.label: Address it head-on, loudly
options.text: You kill the rumor by confronting it directly. It's a bit of a scene, and everyone's talking about it now.

options.label: Ignore it, let it die on its own
options.text: It fades in a week or two, same as most gym gossip does. Nobody remembers who started it.

prompt: A longtime training partner announces he's leaving for a rival gym, mid-camp.

options.label: Make it a public falling-out
options.text: The gym takes a side, loudly, and the story travels well past the parking lot.

options.label: Wish him well and move on quietly
options.text: It stings, but the room stays calm and everyone keeps their focus on camp.

prompt: A confident new hire at the gym starts openly angling for your spot as top dog.

options.label: Put him in his place in sparring
options.text: You make your point clearly, in front of everyone. It's effective and it's a little ugly.

options.label: Let your results do the talking instead
options.text: You don't engage the posturing at all. The room notices the restraint more than you'd expect.

prompt: Someone at the gym leaks your fight-week weight to a rival's camp.

options.label: Call it out publicly, find who did it
options.text: It turns into a whole thing. You get your answer, and the gym spends a few tense days afterward.

options.label: Let it go, focus on the fight instead
options.text: You don't chase it down. Whoever did it never gets called out, and camp stays calm.

prompt: Your sibling's wedding lands right in the middle of camp.

options.label: Go, help pay for the flight, be fully present
options.text: It costs you time and money, but you're standing there when it matters, not making excuses over the phone.

options.label: Send your regrets, stay in camp
options.text: You keep every session on schedule. The family group chat is a little quieter around you for a while.

prompt: A parent calls, quietly asking for help covering a bill this month.

options.label: Send the money without a second thought
options.text: It's not a huge amount, but it's exactly what was needed, and you can hear the relief in their voice.

options.label: Explain camp has you stretched thin right now
options.text: You're not wrong about the timing. It doesn't make the conversation feel any better.

prompt: A family reunion falls the week before the fight, and everyone's expecting you there.

options.label: Go for the day, help cover the catering
options.text: It's a long day and an unplanned expense, but the whole family gets to see you before fight night.

options.label: Stay in camp, skip it entirely
options.text: You protect the final week completely. Someone records a video message for you to watch later.

prompt: Your kid's school play is the same night as a session you can't easily move.

options.label: Skip the session, be in the front row
options.text: You miss a round of training you'll never notice was gone. The look on their face when they spot you is worth it.

options.label: Stay in the gym, catch the recording later
options.text: The session goes as planned. Watching it back on a phone screen isn't quite the same.

prompt: Family asks you to fly home for a holiday right in the middle of a demanding camp block.

options.label: Book the flight, cover the cost yourself
options.text: It's an expensive detour, but being home, even briefly, resets something camp had been wearing down.

options.label: Stay put, call in for the holiday instead
options.text: You keep training uninterrupted. The call is warm, but it's not the same as being there.

prompt: A rival calls you out online, tagging every account that'll amplify it.

options.label: Clap back publicly, keep it sharp
options.text: The exchange goes semi-viral by evening. It's exactly the kind of noise that sells a future fight.

options.label: Stay silent, let the callout sit there unanswered
options.text: It's the boring, professional choice. The sponsor's marketing team is quietly relieved.

prompt: At a public weigh-in for another card, a rival starts talking trash directly at you from the crowd.

options.label: Fire back in front of everyone
options.text: It's a scene, and it's clipped and shared within the hour. Everyone's talking about the eventual matchup now.

options.label: Smile and walk past without a word
options.text: It reads as ice-cold on camera. Some people love it, some people wanted more fireworks.

prompt: A rival's team tries to bait you into a street confrontation outside a local event.

options.label: Engage — let it get heated
options.text: Nothing physical happens, but the shouting match ends up all over local sports pages by morning.

options.label: Walk away, refuse to take the bait
options.text: You leave without incident. It's not a dramatic story, but it's the smart one.

prompt: A rival's manager offers a "friendly" open sparring session that's obviously meant to bait a real confrontation.

options.label: Accept, on your own terms
options.text: The session goes exactly as hard as everyone expected. Footage of it ends up everywhere.

options.label: Decline the invitation entirely
options.text: You don't engage the setup at all. It's a quiet non-story, which is exactly the point.

prompt: A clip surfaces of a rival mocking your last performance in detail, tagged everywhere.

options.label: Post a sharp response of your own
options.text: The back-and-forth builds real heat for whenever this matchup actually happens.

options.label: Don't dignify it with a response
options.text: You let the clip run its course without adding fuel. It fades faster than a real feud would.

prompt: Your coach wants one more hard round out of you when you're already visibly gassed.

options.label: Grind through the extra round
options.text: You finish it on fumes. The room clocks the effort, and it means something later.

options.label: Tell him you're done for the day
options.text: You end the session early. It's the right call for recovery, even if it doesn't feel heroic.

prompt: The coach suggests skipping tomorrow's session entirely to avoid burning out this deep in camp.

options.label: Insist on training anyway
options.text: You get the extra work in. Whether your body thanks you for it later is an open question.

options.label: Take the rest day he's offering
options.text: You come back the next day sharper than you'd have been otherwise.

prompt: Your coach wants to try a new, unproven training method this deep into camp.

options.label: Commit fully, trust the process
options.text: It's rough on your body while you adjust, but the crew respects that you didn't second-guess him out loud.

options.label: Push back, stick with what's worked
options.text: You keep your routine intact. He drops it without much argument, but you can tell it landed a little.

prompt: The coach wants to bring in a specialist for a weak spot in your game — it'll eat serious time this week.

options.label: Clear the schedule and dive in
options.text: It's an exhausting few days of very specific, very necessary work.

options.label: Push it to a later, less packed week
options.text: You protect this week's schedule. The weak spot stays exactly where it was.

prompt: The coach asks you to mentor a younger fighter, which means splitting your own training time.

options.label: Say yes and make real time for it
options.text: It costs you noticeable training time, and the gym takes real notice of the gesture.

options.label: Decline, protect your own camp
options.text: You keep every minute for yourself this camp. The younger fighter finds guidance somewhere else.

prompt: A local charity asks if you'll make an appearance at their fundraiser this weekend.

options.label: Go, give them the full afternoon
options.text: It eats a chunk of your weekend, but you leave the event genuinely glad you went.

options.label: Send a signed item instead of showing up
options.text: It's a smaller gesture, but it protects the whole weekend for camp.

prompt: A children's hospital asks if you'd be willing to visit for an afternoon.

options.label: Clear the afternoon and go
options.text: It's the kind of afternoon that puts the rest of camp in perspective.

options.label: Decline, stay locked into camp
options.text: You protect the training block. The hospital finds someone else for this one.

prompt: Your coach's old gym asks you to headline a benefit exhibition for the neighborhood.

options.label: Headline it, no hesitation
options.text: It's a long night in front of a crowd that means something to your coach personally.

options.label: Pass, protect the training calendar
options.text: You keep the week intact. Your coach doesn't push, but you can tell he'd hoped for a yes.

prompt: A youth fundraiser wants a signed item for their auction and, ideally, you in person for an hour.

options.label: Show up for the full hour
options.text: The item sells for more than expected, and a room full of kids gets a photo with you.

options.label: Ship the signed item, skip the appearance
options.text: The auction still goes fine without you there. It's a smaller story either way.

prompt: A community center asks you to speak to a room of teenagers about staying out of trouble.

options.label: Go and actually mean it
options.text: You end up staying longer than planned, answering questions nobody expected you to take seriously.

options.label: Decline this time around
options.text: You keep the afternoon for training. The center understands, and asks again next camp.
